In what year was Andromeda Galaxy discovered?
Andromeda Galaxy: The Andromeda Galaxy is a barred spiral galaxy and is the nearest major galaxy to the Milky Way.
Pillars of Creation: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. The astronomers responsible for the photo were Jeff Hester and Paul Scowen from Arizona State University.
Which company manufactures KAI T-50 Golden Eagle?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Korea Aerospace Industries. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
In which country is Convair B-58 Hustler based?
Convair B-58 Hustler: United States. The Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight.
Who is credited with discovering Rutherfordium?
Rutherfordium: Albert Ghiorso. Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.
Who is credited with discovering Ampère's force law?
Ampère's force law: André-Marie Ampère. In magnetostatics, Ampère's force law describes the force of attraction or repulsion between two current-carrying wires.
Who is credited with discovering Rhenium?
Rhenium: Walter Noddack. Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.
Often confused with the unrelated sweet chestnut, this large deciduous tree in the maple, soapberry, and lychee family bears hermaphroditic flowers — what tree is it?
Aesculus hippocastanum is a species of flowering plant in the maple, soapberry and lychee family Sapindaceae.
A member of the aminopenicillin family usually swallowed by mouth, this go-to remedy for ear infections, strep throat, and pneumonia is often paired with clavulanic acid — which antibiotic is it?
Amoxicillin is an antibiotic medication belonging to the aminopenicillin class of the penicillin family.
Its Latin name means 'water-carrier,' and this zodiac constellation sits between Capricornus and Pisces, in a region of the sky nicknamed 'the Sea' for its watery neighbors — which constellation?

Aquarius (constellation) is an equatorial constellation of the zodiac, between Capricornus and Pisces. Its name is Latin for "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier", and its traditional astrological symbol is (♒︎), a representation of water.
Derived from a particular acid, this class of depressant drugs once treated anxiety and insomnia, but their overdose risk got them largely replaced by benzodiazepines and 'Z-drugs' — what are they?
Barbiturate are a class of depressant drugs that are chemically derived from barbituric acid.
Represented most commonly as a 1 or a 0, this portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most fundamental unit of information in computing — what is it called?
Bit is the most basic unit of information in computing and digital communication.
One of only two elements liquid at room temperature, this reddish-brown, pungent-smelling element takes its name from the Greek word for 'stench.' What element is it (symbol Br)?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Standardized worldwide in 1907 as exactly 200 milligrams, this unit of mass is used to weigh gemstones and pearls, and is divisible into 100 smaller 'points' — what unit is it?
Carat (mass) (ct) is a unit of mass equal to 200 mg (0.00705 oz; 0.00643 ozt), which is used for measuring gemstones and pearls.
This woody perennial herb with bright blue flowers is cultivated for salad greens and a root that's roasted and ground as a coffee substitute. What plant is it?
Chicory (Cichorium intybus) is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant of the family Asteraceae, usually with bright blue flowers, rarely white or pink.
More closely related to lungfish and land vertebrates than to ordinary ray-finned fish, this ancient lobe-finned fish survives today as a single genus with just two known species — which fish?
Coelacanth are an ancient group of lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii) in the class Actinistia.
Affecting roughly 1 in 22,000 births and more common in girls, which genetic condition caused by a chromosome 5 deletion takes its French name from a feline-sounding cry?
Cri du chat syndrome is a rare genetic disorder due to a partial chromosome deletion on chromosome 5.
This colourless, highly volatile, sweet-smelling organic compound with formula (CH3CH2)2O was once used as a general anesthetic and remains a common laboratory solvent — what is it?

This American theoretical physicist, a professor emeritus at Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study, is renowned for foundational contributions to string theory and topological quantum field theory — who is he?
Edward Witten (born August 26, 1951) is an American theoretical physicist known for his contributions to string theory, topological quantum field theory, and various areas of mathematics.
The major female sex hormone, this estrogen steroid drives the development of breasts and a female pattern of fat distribution and regulates the menstrual cycle — which one is it?
Estradiol (E2), also called oestrogen, oestradiol, is an estrogen steroid hormone and the major female sex hormone.

Sometimes mistakenly called a cat despite belonging to the weasel family, this North American forest-dwelling carnivore is the only living species in its genus and is larger than the martens it resembles — what animal is it?
Fisher (animal) (Pekania pennanti) is a carnivorous mammal native to North America, a forest-dwelling creature whose range covers much of the boreal forest in Canada to the northern United States.
Its name literally means 'Earth writing,' and it explores not just where things are but how they changed and came to be across the planet — what field is it?
Geography (from Ancient Greek geographia; combining ge 'Earth' and graphein 'write', lit. 'Earth writing') is the study of the lands, features, inhabitants, and phenomena of planet Earth.
Nicknamed the 'benevolent dictator for life' of the language he invented, this Dutch programmer relinquished that title in July 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum (born 31 January 1956) is a Dutch programmer.
This genus of the mallow family includes several hundred species prized for their large, showy blooms, and is sometimes known by the alternate name rose mallow — name the genus?
Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
Prized in folk medicine as an antiseptic and expectorant, this Lamiaceae shrub grows wild from Southern Europe to the Caspian Sea area — which plant is it?
Hyssopus officinalis is a shrub in the Lamiaceae or mint family native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the region surrounding the Caspian Sea.

This English mathematician made foundational contributions to matrix and invariant theory, founded the American Journal of Mathematics at Johns Hopkins, and was teaching at Oxford when he died. Who was he?
James Joseph Sylvester (3 September 1814 - 15 March 1897) was an English mathematician.
This Indian aerospace engineer served as secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of both ISRO and the Space Commission — who is he?
K. Sivan (born 14 April 1957) is an Indian aerospace engineer who served as the secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of ISRO and Space Commission.
Closely related to earthworms but equipped with a sucker at each end, these segmented parasitic or predatory worms make up their own subclass within the annelid phylum — what are they?
Leech are segmented parasitic or predatory worms that comprise the subclass Hirudinea within the phylum Annelida.
Based on a commercial airliner design, this four-engine turboprop aircraft hunts submarines for the U.S. Navy using a distinctive tail-mounted magnetic detector — what plane is it?
Lockheed P-3 Orion is a four-engined, turboprop anti-submarine and maritime surveillance aircraft developed for the United States Navy and introduced in the 1960s.

With over 2,400 species sporting triangular heads, bulging eyes on flexible necks, and folded forelegs built to snatch prey, these insects count termites and cockroaches among their closest relatives — what are they?
Mantis are an order (Mantodea) of insects that contains over 2,400 species in about 460 genera in 33 families.

This chemical compound, typically administered by vein injection, is primarily used to treat methemoglobinemia and was used for over a century against malaria. Common side effects include headache, nausea, and vomiting. What is it?
Methylene blue is a salt used as a dye and as a medication.
This Bangladeshi economist pioneered microcredit and founded Grameen Bank, work that earned him the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize before he later led an interim government — who is he?
Muhammad Yunus (born 28 June 1940) is a Bangladeshi economist and statesman.

Discovered in a fossil-rich West African formation and first described in 1976 but not formally named until 1999, this rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur lived roughly 115 to 105 million years ago — which genus?
Nigersaurus is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived during the middle Cretaceous period, about 115 to 105 million years ago.
This specialized subunit within a biological cell performs a specific function, and may be enclosed in its own membrane or exist without one. What is it?
Organelle is a specialized subunit, within a biological cell, that has a specific function.
Known in the US as a goober and in the UK as a monkey nut, this Fabaceae crop hides its edible seeds in underground pods. What is it?

Peanut (Arachis hypogaea), also known as the groundnut, goober (US, via Kikongo), goober pea, pindar (US, via Kikongo) or monkey nut (UK), is a legume crop grown mainly for its edible seeds, contained in underground pods.
Native to Chile and Peru and cultivated since Inca times, this nightshade fruit is known in English as the Cape gooseberry or goldenberry — what is its scientific name?
Physalis peruviana is a species of plant in the nightshade family (Solanaceae) native to Chile and Peru.
A strongly alkaline, water-soluble salt of carbonic acid, which compound with the formula K2CO3 is used in glassmaking and Dutch-process chocolate?
Potassium carbonate is the inorganic compound with the formula K2CO3. It is deliquescent, often appearing as a damp or wet solid.
One of America's top rocketry and high-speed-flight experts, this engineer helped found engineering cybernetics before being deported to China in 1955. Who was he?

Qian Xuesen (December 11, 1911 - October 31, 2009; also spelled as Tsien Hsue-shen) was a Chinese aerospace engineer and cyberneticist who made significant contributions to the field of aerodynamics and established engineering cybernetics.
With Patrick Steptoe and Jean Purdy, this British physiologist pioneered the technique that led to the 1978 birth of Louise Brown, earning a 2010 Nobel Prize. Who was he?
Robert Edwards (physiologist) (27 September 1925 - 10 April 2013) was a British physiologist and pioneer in reproductive medicine, and in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) in particular.

Often striking suddenly after heavy lifting and described as a shooting pain down one leg, about 90% of cases trace to a spinal disc herniation pressing on a nerve root — what's this condition called?
Sciatica is pain going down the leg from the lower back.
Long, thin and transparent, this hydrozoan drifts through the ocean as a colony of specialized zooids that together handle feeding, floating and jet propulsion — what marine organism is this?
Siphonophore (from Ancient Greek (siphn), meaning "tube" and - (-phros), meaning "bearing") are cnidarian animals of the hydrozoan order Siphonophorae.
Haunted by the Holocaust and the Eichmann trial, this American social psychologist ran his notorious obedience experiments in a Yale basement in 1961. Who was he?
Stanley Milgram (August 15, 1933 - December 20, 1984) was an American social psychologist who conducted controversial experiments on obedience in the 1960s during his professorship at Yale.
Appointed a government economic minister in 1991, this academic rose to become prime minister of Turkey in 1993 and later served as its foreign minister — who is she?
Tansu Çiller (born 24 May 1946) is a Turkish academic, economist, and politician who served as the 22nd prime minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996.
The largest member of the genus Panthera and an apex predator of Asian forests, this big cat wears orange fur striped in mostly-vertical black — what is it?
Tiger (Panthera tigris) is a large cat and a member of the genus Panthera native to Asia.
With 92 protons and half-lives stretching up to 4.5 billion years, this radioactive metal is handy for dating the age of the Earth — which silvery-grey element?
Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.
This German hunting-dog breed, recognized in 1891, is so much a working dog that in its homeland it's considered unsuitable simply as a house pet — name the breed?
Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.
Also known as the empirical guideline, this statistical shorthand describes the percentage of values within one, two, and three standard deviations of the mean in a normal distribution — which one?
Transmitted by the bite of an infected tsetse fly, this parasitic infection caused by Trypanosoma brucei is better known in humans as 'sleeping sickness' — what's its formal name?
African trypanosomiasis: Parasitic disease also known as sleeping sickness.

This exaggerated immune response occurs when the body mistakes a harmless substance for a threat, triggering histamine release from mast cells and conditions like hay fever or anaphylaxis. What is this reaction called?
Allergy: Immune system response to a substance that most people tolerate well.
Considered the father of the exact and natural sciences in Armenia, this 7th-century polymath wrote the first known Armenian geographic work — who was he?
Lacking a tail due to a mutation in the TBXT gene, this superfamily of primates includes gibbons as the 'lesser' branch and humans among the 'great' branch — which animal group?
Ape: Superfamily of primates. The family Hylobatidae, the lesser apes, include four genera and a total of 20 species of gibbon, including the lar gibbon and the siamang, all native to Asia.
Larger than a meteoroid but smaller than a planet, most of these rocky, metallic, or icy bodies orbit between Mars and Jupiter — what are they called?
Asteroid: Minor planet found within the inner Solar System.
Named by naturalist Constantine Rafinesque in 1815, this predatory saltwater fish prowls near coral reefs and is a favorite target of sport anglers worldwide — what is it?
This interdisciplinary field examines moral questions raised by advances in biology, medicine, and biotechnology, touching everything from patient care to environmental policy — what is it called?
Bioethics: Study of the ethical issues emerging from advances in biology and medicine.

Bred in South Africa as a family guard dog, this large mastiff-type breed has a short coat and heavy bone structure, and is recognized by that country's kennel union but not the international federation — what breed is it?
Boerboel: South African breed of dog. The Boerboel (pronounced [ˈbuːrbul]) is a South African breed of large dog of mastiff type, used as a family guard dog.
An intact, more muscular and aggressive adult male of the cattle species, this animal has long been a sacrificial symbol in many religions and stars in famous arena sports. What is it?
Bull: Adult male cattle. A bull is an intact (i.e., not castrated) adult male of the species Bos taurus (cattle).
Indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains and grown across Asia and Africa largely for hashish production, this plant species carries far more THC than industrial hemp — which species is it?
Cannabis indica: Species of plant. Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Its edible 'curd' is actually a dense head of undeveloped flower buds, and one variety grows its curds in spiral fractal patterns — which vegetable?
Cauliflower: Vegetable in the species Brassica oleracea.
Native to the high Andes and living in colonies called 'herds,' this South American rodent boasts the densest fur of any land mammal — about 20,000 hairs per square centimeter. What is it?
Chinchilla: Rodent genus. The chinchilla is named after the Chincha people of the Andes, who once wore its dense, velvet-like fur and ate its meat.
Discovered in 1969 and sold under the brand name Lotrimin, this azole-class medication treats athlete's foot, ringworm, and oral thrush — what is it?

Native to the western Palearctic and closely related to the rock dove, this large bird feeds mainly on cereals and other plant matter, making it an agricultural pest despite being heavily hunted across its range — what is it?
Common wood pigeon: Species of large, white/green-naped, arboreal bird of Eurasia.
Unknown in the wild, this cultivated autumn-flowering plant has had its dried stigmas prized as the world's priciest spice for over 3,500 years — what is its scientific name?
Crocus sativus: Species of flowering plant. Crocus sativus, commonly known as saffron crocus or autumn crocus, is a species of flowering plant in the iris family Iridaceae.
Introduced in 1984, this turboprop regional airliner series was developed from an earlier company model and later gained 'Quiet' variants with active noise-cancellation — which aircraft family?

De Havilland Canada Dash 8: Canadian turboprop airliner. The De Havilland Canada DHC-8, commonly known as the Dash 8, is a series of turboprop-powered regional airliners, introduced by de Havilland Canada (DHC) in 1984.

The largest collection of fossils from this extinct Ice Age canine came from the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles, though it roamed from South American savanna to North American forested mountains — what animal was it?
Dire wolf: Extinct species of canine mammal.
Its name comes from the Greek word for 'house,' and it studies organisms from the level of a single individual all the way up to the entire biosphere — which branch of biology is it?
Ecology: Study of organisms and their environment.

This is the process of creating economic value by spotting and commercializing opportunities — typically demanding considerable initiative and bearing real risk in exchange for most of the reward. What's the term?
Entrepreneurship: Taking financial risks in the hope of profit.
Also known by the scientific name Gyps fulvus, this large Old World bird of prey belongs to the family Accipitridae — which species is it?
Eurasian griffon vulture: Species of bird. It is also known as the Eurasian griffon or griffon vulture, although the latter term is sometimes used for the genus Gyps as a whole.
This centuries-old number theory statement claims there are no positive whole-number solutions to a^n + b^n = c^n whenever the exponent exceeds two — what's it called?
Fermat's Last Theorem: 17th-century conjecture proved by Andrew Wiles in 1994.
Marked by physical traits such as a long face, large ears, and unusually flexible fingers, this inherited neurodevelopmental disorder stems from a repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene — which condition?
Fragile X syndrome: X-linked dominant genetic disorder.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, these lizards are unusual for making vocal chirps and clicks, and most lack eyelids, relying on a transparent membrane instead — what are they?
Gecko: Lizards belonging to the suborder Gekkota.
One of the very first animals domesticated — in Iran some 10,000 years ago — this Bovidae cousin of the sheep now numbers over 1.1 billion worldwide, 150 million of them in India; what is it?

This French civil engineer made his name building railway bridges like the Garabit Viaduct and later helped erect the Statue of Liberty, before retiring to study meteorology and aerodynamics — who was he?

A pioneer of modern control theory whose collaboration with Claude Shannon helped lay the foundations of the Information Age, he also helped design the automatic guns that defended London from V-1 flying bombs — who was he?
Hendrik Wade Bode: American scientist and engineer (1905–1982)
A pungent root vegetable in the same family as mustard, wasabi, and cabbage, this spice is likely native to Southeastern Europe and Western Asia — what is it?
Horseradish: Species of flowering plants in the cabbage family Brassicaceae.
This mammal order today includes only small African and Middle Eastern hyraxes, but once boasted a species weighing up to 600 kilograms called Titanohyrax — which order?
Hyracoidea: Order of mammals. It includes the living hyraxes, placed within the family Procaviidae, and several extinct taxa.
She and her husband won the 1935 Nobel in Chemistry for discovering induced radioactivity — making her half of the only mother-daughter pair to both win Nobel Prizes. Who is this scientist?
Irène Joliot-Curie: French chemist and physicist (1897–1956)

This temporary condition throws your internal body clock out of sync with local time after rapid travel across multiple time zones — and most people find it harder to shake off flying east than west — what is it?

Jet lag: Condition due to travel across time zones. The phase shift when travelling from east to west is referred to as phase-delay of the circadian cycle, whereas going west to east is phase-advance of the cycle.

Known to NATO by the reporting name Hokum A and nicknamed 'Black Shark' for its distinctive coaxial rotors, this Russian single-seat attack helicopter has a rare rescue ejection system — which aircraft?
Kamov Ka-50: Attack helicopter. It was designed in the 1980s and adopted for service in the Russian army in 1995.

Native to the tropical Americas, this flowering shrub was carried to Europe by Dutch explorers and later brought to Goa by the Portuguese, becoming a notorious invasive weed across some 50 countries — which plant?
Lantana camara: Species of plant. Lantana camara (common lantana) is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family (Verbenaceae), native to the tropics of the Americas.
Also called May bells or Our Lady's tears, this woodland plant's sweetly scented white bell-flowers hide a dangerously poisonous secret — which flower?
Lily of the valley: Species of flowering plant in the asparagus family.
This best-known stag beetle species in Western Europe lends its genus its very name, and is currently listed as Near Threatened — what is it?
Lucanus cervus: Species of beetle. L. cervus is listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN Red List.

One of the most colorful mammals alive, this West African monkey sports vivid red-and-blue facial skin and lives in huge groups called 'hordes' — though long mistaken for a baboon, it's actually closer kin to mangabeys. What is it?
Mandrill: Species of Old World monkey from Africa.

This elephant-sized extinct genus of South American ground sloths, whose type species weighed up to four tonnes, was first identified from a fossil found on an Argentine riverbank in 1787 — which genus?
Megatherium: Genus of extinct ground sloth. The first (holotype) specimen of Megatherium americanum was discovered in 1787 on the bank of the Luján River in what is now northern Argentina.
Sold as Versed, this benzodiazepine sedates rather than knocks you out, can be sprayed up the nose or squirted in the cheek, and famously causes anterograde amnesia — which drug?
Midazolam: Benzodiazepine used for anesthesia and procedural sedation.
This rounded mound of fatty tissue overlies the junction where the two pubic bones meet — what is it?
Mons pubis: Rounded mass of fatty tissue found over the pubic symphysis.

The first production helicopter with fully fly-by-wire flight controls, this European twin-engine military chopper comes in troop-transport and naval anti-submarine variants flown by over a dozen NATO nations. What is it?
NHIndustries NH90: Family of military helicopters.
Surrounded by a typically darker-colored areola, this raised region of breast tissue is where milk exits through the lactiferous ducts during lactation — what is it?
Nipple: Part of the breast. The milk can flow through the nipple passively, or it can be ejected by smooth muscle contractions that occur along with the ductal system.
First described in 1689 by a local naturalist, this aquatic cave-dwelling salamander is the only exclusively cave-dwelling chordate native to Europe — what is it?
Britain, Germany, and Italy jointly built this twin-engine, variable-sweep-wing combat jet through a tri-national consortium, first flying it in 1974 — which aircraft?
Panavia Tornado: Family of multi-role combat aircraft.

Caused by a lack of vitamin B3 (niacin), this disease is remembered for its grim quartet of symptoms — inflamed skin, diarrhea, dementia, and mouth sores — striking sun-exposed skin first. What is it?
Pellagra: Human disease caused by a lack of vitamin B3. The two main types of pellagra are primary and secondary.
With a phosphate-charged head and two fatty-acid tails joined by glycerol, this molecule builds neuron membranes and can decline up to 20% by age 80 — what is it?

Its methods range from gentle negotiation and lawmaking all the way to warfare against adversaries, and the social science that studies it tacks 'science' onto its name; what is this activity of settling a society's affairs?
Politics: Activities associated with group decisions.
Discovered in 1915, this red dwarf is the closest star to Earth besides the Sun, orbiting its two larger neighbors once every 550,000 years — which star?
Proxima Centauri: Nearest star to the Solar System.
Used to treat malaria resistant to chloroquine, this bitter compound also flavors tonic water and can cause ringing in the ears at high doses — what is it?
Quinine: Medication used to treat malaria and babesiosis.
Aristotle called this ancient art 'the faculty of observing the available means of persuasion,' identifying logos, pathos, and ethos as its three key appeals — which discipline?
Rhetoric: Art of persuasion. It is one of the three ancient arts of discourse (trivium) of classical antiquity, along with grammar and logic/dialectic.

Named after the naturalist who first studied it and described in 1797, this extremely venomous South Asian snake is notorious for its excruciatingly painful bite and ranks among the region's 'Big Four' — what snake is it?
Russell's viper: Species of venomous snake. Russell's viper (Daboia russelii) is a species of highly venomous snake in the family Viperidae.
Driven by an empirical cycle of observation, hypothesis, testing, and conclusion, this systematic discipline splits into natural and social branches. What is it?
Science: Systematic endeavour to gain knowledge.
Native to East Asia, this cultivated mushroom is also known as the black mushroom or Chinese mushroom — name the fungus?

Known as sun spiders, camel spiders, or wind scorpions, this arachnid order is neither true spider nor scorpion, and urban legends wildly exaggerate its size, speed, and danger to humans — what is it?
Solifugae: Order of arachnids. The order includes more than 1,000 described species in about 147 genera.
Fired by Apple's board in 1985, he founded NeXT and bought a animation studio before returning a decade later to revolutionize consumer tech. Who?
Steve Jobs: American businessman and inventor (1955–2011)
This Polish tax advisor turned politician placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing the libertarian New Hope party — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen: Polish economist and politician (born 1986)
This group of inherited blood disorders reduces hemoglobin production and is classified as alpha or beta depending on which globin gene is deficient. What condition is it?
Thalassemia: Family of inherited blood disorders. Symptoms depend on the type of thalassemia and can vary from none to severe, including death.
Also known as the Mexican husk tomato, this nightshade fruit has been cultivated since pre-Columbian times and is the key ingredient in salsa verde — what is it?

This large flatfish native to the Northeast Atlantic, Baltic, and Mediterranean gave its name to a 1990s fishing dispute between Canada and Spain, even though a different species was the real catch at stake — which fish?
Turbot: Species of flatfish in the family Scophthalmidae.
This hairy biennial plant can top two meters, packing small yellow flowers onto a tall spike that sprouts from a low leaf rosette in disturbed, sunlit soil — which weedy species?
Verbascum thapsus: Species of plant. It is a hairy biennial plant that can grow to 2 m tall or more.
First isolated in 1669 by alchemist Henning Brand, this waxy, translucent form of an element glows faintly green in the dark and ignites spontaneously in air — which substance?
Tracing its formal origins to Aristotle and later shaped by Carl Linnaeus, this branch of biology studies the structure, classification and behavior of animals — which field?
The symbol for hassium is Hs. Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
The symbol for actinium is Ac. Actinium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ac and atomic number 89.

Drew Barrymore: Drew Blythe Barrymore (born February 22, 1975) is an American actress, producer, talk show host, and businesswoman.

Richard Harris: Richard St John Francis Harris (1 October 1930 – 25 October 2002) was an Irish actor and singer.
